To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a methodology to combine different data sets to reconstruct atmospheric profiles of wet refrativity and that we have validated the reconstruction quality by comparing to radiosonde measurements.

the combination of GPS zenith path delay, ground measurements of pressure, temperature, and humidity, and microwave radiometer temperature profiles allows us to reconstruct wet refractivity profiles and dew point temperature profiles with a high accuracy in the lower tropospheric layer.

we have developed an approach that reconstructs atmospheric wet refractivity and dew point temperature profiles at high vertical and temporal resolution from data of the global positioning system (GPS), ground meteorological measurements (surface pressure and temperature), microwave radiometer temperature profiles and radio occultation measurements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reconstruction of humidity profiles in the lower tropospheric layers.
the combination and validation of data sets for the retrieval of atmospheric wet refractivity and dew point temperature profiles in the lower troposhere.

the combination of data sets of wet tropospheric refractivity from ground-based measurements, GPS and radio occultation, to reconstruct near-continuous humidity profiles in the western part of the Swiss plateau.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of the various available data sets is a valuable and necessary tool to improve our knowledge about the atmosphere.

the combination of the data sets is beneficial for the reconstruction of the wet refractive index, and that it is beneficial for the conversion from wet refraction index to relative humidity, but not for the conversion to dew point temperature.
this study is a first step towards an operational nowcasting tool for humidity profiles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of data sets is a promising approach to obtain atmospheric humidity profiles with high vertical and temporal resolution.
we have demonstrated the possibility of reconstructing humidity profiles in the lower tropo- sphere from the combination of different remote sensing data sets.

the collocation approach with a combination of data sets of different types is a powerful tool for the reconstruction of atmospheric profiles, and it can be used for nowcasting of humidity and clouds.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can reconstruct wet refractivity profiles with a high degree of accuracy and that the combination of different data sets is crucial for this.

a data fusion approach combining GPS and ground measurements is very useful for the reconstruction of wet refractivity profiles and that the combination with radio occultation measurements is beneficial for the upper troposphere, while the addition of radiometer temperature profiles allows to derive near-continuous dewpoint temperature profiles at Payern.
a combination of different data sets is superior to the individual data sets in the quality of the reconstructed profiles.
